name: Dead Colt Creek Recreation Area
note: Ransom County recreation area ~5 miles SE of Lisbon on the Dead Colt Creek reservoir; partial 20/30/50-amp electric hookups, dump station and bath house plus tent sites, with a swimming beach and fishing. Open May-Sept; sites reservable (Roverpass) with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Parkhurst Campground (Pipestem Lake)
note: Stutsman County Park Board rec area on the north side of Pipestem Dam/Reservoir (USACE dam) ~5 miles N of Jamestown. Primitive designated RV sites, pit/vault toilets, dump station, boat ramps and a horse area (corrals/tethers) — first-come, first-served, honor system. --Claude

name: Parshall Bay Recreation Area
note: Mountrail County recreation area on the NE corner of Lake Sakakawea's Van Hook Arm (Parshall Bay), ~100 campsites across three sections — ~50 electric hookups plus primitive camping — with showerhouse, vault toilets, three boat ramps, fish-cleaning stations and playgrounds. Mostly first-come, first-served (mid-May-mid-Sept); 12 long-term/seasonal spots reservable. --Claude

name: Tolna City Park
note: Tolna municipal park (N end of town off Hwy 15). RV sites with electric+water hookups, bathrooms and showers; first-come, first-served ($40/week). --Claude

name: Tolna Dam
note: Nelson County rec area at Tolna Dam, 1 mi S + 2 mi E of Tolna on Hwy 15, on the dam's reservoir (Sheyenne River overflow). Rustic camping with power, shelter, vault toilet, and boat ramp/dock; first-come, first-served, free-will donation. --Claude

name: Logan State Park
note: MT state park on the north shore of Middle Thompson Lake, ~45 mi SE of Libby on Hwy 2; heavily forested. 30 sites reservable via ReserveAmerica, 7 FCFS. --Claude

name: Clark Canyon Reservoir, Lewis & Clark Campground
note: Developed Bureau of Reclamation campground and marina area at Clark Canyon Reservoir on the Beaverhead River, ~20 mi S of Dillon off I-15. Lewis & Clark is the one hookup loop of the reservoir's campgrounds, paid at a self-pay station (~$30/night); vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramp and courtesy dock. The other Clark Canyon campgrounds are free and first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Bolster Dam Campgrounds
note: City of Plentywood campground on the north edge of town below the Bolster Dam reservoir; 18 sites with 30-amp electric (seasonal water), picnic tables, fire rings, outhouses and a boat ramp; big rigs accepted. Open year-round, no reservations, self-pay station (bring cash) — first-come, first-served. Free fishing/paddling on the reservoir. --Claude

name: Rexford Bench Campground
note: Kootenai NF, on an arm of Lake Koocanusa near Rexford, 7 mi from Eureka; ponderosa pine at ~2,470 ft. High- and low-water boat ramps, fish-cleaning stations, swim beach, interpretive loop and the Hoodoo Trail to sandstone formations. The beach/recreation area above the high-water mark (with its flush restrooms) and the Kamloops overflow parking are closed for water/wastewater system work from July 13 until October 30, 2026; the campground stays open (Forest Service alert, read 2026-10-22). --Claude

name: Barretts Park Campground
note: Bureau of Reclamation campground and boat take-out on the Beaverhead River, ~5 mi S of Dillon at I-15 exit 56; ~10 tent/trailer sites, picnic tables, fire rings, drinking water, accessible vault toilets, 14-day limit. First-come, first-served (no reservation system). RV inspection notes sites up to ~45 ft. --Claude

name: Curt Gowdy State Park (Aspen Grove Campground)
note: Curt Gowdy SP between Cheyenne and Laramie has 159 sites in 12 areas around Granite & Crystal reservoirs; 44 sites w/ 50-amp electric+water (Tumbleweeds, Crystal), rest dry; RVs to ~50 ft; dump station. Pinned at Aspen Grove loop (13 dry sites, rigs to ~39 ft, adjacent to a public horse corral). 90 reservable / 69 FCFS. --Claude

name: White Mountain Road Dispersed Camping
note: BLM (Rock Springs FO) dispersed camping along White Mountain Road N of Green River/Rock Springs, near the Wild Horse Scenic Loop and White Mountain petroglyphs. Graded gravel/dirt road passable to 2WD; no defined sites, no services; drive-in dispersed. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Atlantic City Campground
note: BLM Lander FO campground near the historic town of Atlantic City / South Pass. 18 sites among trees, a few pull-throughs, most fit RVs to ~30 ft; vault toilets, seasonal water, tables, fire rings; no dump. First-come, first-served, ~Jun 1-Oct 31. --Claude

name: Pete's Draw Campground
note: BLM Casper FO campground on the North Platte River (Grey Reef-Lusby reach) near Alcova. 7 overnight sites, each with table, fire ring, shelter, tent pad and RV parking space; vault toilet; no water/hookups. $10/night, first-come, first-served, 14-day limit; float/fishing access. --Claude

name: Teton Reservoir Campground
note: BLM Rawlins Field Office recreation site ~13 mi south of Rawlins off WY-71. First-come, first-served: 5 campsites with picnic tables, fire rings and parking spurs (no pull-throughs), vault toilets and a boat ramp on Teton Reservoir. Use season ~June 1-Nov 15; access roads turn to mud when wet. --Claude

name: Fontenelle Creek Campground
note: BLM Kemmerer Field Office campground on the west side of Fontenelle Reservoir, ~30 mi north of Kemmerer off US-189. 55 campsites with covered tables and grills, potable water, vault + flush restrooms, dump station and boat ramp; paved roads. Both FCFS and reservable online; ~$7/night. --Claude

name: Gray Reef Reservoir
note: Bureau of Reclamation land on the North Platte River below Gray Reef Dam, managed by Natrona County Parks; ~30 mi SW of Casper via Hwy 220/CR-412. 10 first-come, first-served sites with vault toilets, fishing pier and boat ramp; no hookups or potable water; sites reported to fit rigs to ~35 ft. --Claude

name: Weeping Rock Campground
note: BLM Kemmerer Field Office campground on the west bank of the Green River just below Fontenelle Dam, upstream of Seedskadee NWR. First-come, first-served with pit toilets, fire rings and direct river access (motorboats prohibited); no potable water - bring your own. BLM runs it for Reclamation. --Claude

name: Slate Creek Campground
note: BLM Kemmerer Field Office campground on the Green River just south of Fontenelle Reservoir and north of Seedskadee NWR. First-come, first-served designated sites with 2 ADA vault toilets and river fishing access; no potable water. --Claude

name: Encampment River Campground
note: BLM Rawlins Field Office campground directly on the Encampment River ~2 mi SW of Encampment. 8 first-come, first-served sites with tables, fire rings, vault toilet and a boat ramp; no potable water; no pull-throughs. Campers report rigs to 25 ft / Class C fit. --Claude

name: Tailrace Campground
note: BLM Kemmerer Field Office camp area on the Green River immediately below Fontenelle Dam, between the reservoir and Seedskadee NWR. First-come, first-served: 3 sites with fire rings and a vault toilet; good birding, fishing and non-motorized boating. --Claude

name: Belle Fourche River Campground (Devils Tower NM)
note: NPS campground along the Belle Fourche River below Devils Tower, shaded by large cottonwoods. 2 loops, 45 sites: 43 pull-through for RVs to 35 ft, plus ADA and tent-group sites; drinking water, restrooms, no hookups. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov for booking); open ~spring to fall. --Claude

name: Mammoth Campground
note: Yellowstone NP campground near Mammoth Hot Springs, 82 sites on a terraced sagebrush hillside, RV-friendly, dump station, no hookups; open year-round (reservable, with FCFS mid-Oct-Apr). Reservable online. --Claude

name: New Fork Lake Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF (Pinedale RD) primitive campground of 16 single sites on the New Fork Lake shore among aspens; FS page states the unpaved access road is passable by passenger car (no 4WD), no drinking water, food storage required, FCFS. Sandy day-use beach adjacent. --Claude

name: Pacific Creek Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF (Blackrock RD) campground at the north end of Pacific Creek Rd near the Teton Wilderness boundary; 7 standard sites + 1 pull-through, vault toilets, no water, bear boxes, and stock corrals (general campground, not horse-only), FCFS. --Claude

name: Pinnacles Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Wind River RD) 21-site campground near Brooks Lake at ~9,200 ft below the Pinnacle Buttes; max spur 32 ft, vault toilets, bear lockers, no potable water (bring your own), FCFS, 16-day limit. --Claude

name: Sacajawea Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF (Big Piney RD) 24-site FCFS campground on Middle Piney Creek just E of Middle Piney Lake; rustic sites listed for vehicles to ~40 ft (best for smaller trailers), vault toilets, drinking water, bear bins, host Jul-Labor Day. Unpaved forest road, 2WD-passable. --Claude

name: Sheffield Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF (Blackrock RD) 11-site primitive FCFS campground near Flagg Ranch / the Snake River bridge; accommodates RVs and tents, vault toilet, no water, bear boxes. Access is a narrow unpaved spur with a concrete-ford creek crossing and overhanging branches - passable but tight for larger rigs. --Claude

name: Sinks Canyon Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Washakie RD), ~8.5 mi south of Lander on WY-131 along the Popo Agie River. 14 sites, vault toilets, hand-pump potable water, bear boxes; max spur ~20 ft (larger motorhomes have used the Sawmill portion). First-come, first-served, 16-day limit. Distinct from the Sinks Canyon STATE PARK campground. --Claude

name: The Narrows Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF on a peninsula at New Fork Lake, edge of the Wind River Range. Single-family sites in aspen; vault toilets, no drinking water, food storage required, unpaved access road, narrow turnarounds (oversized rigs not recommended). Mostly first-come, first-served with 4 sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Turpin Meadow Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF (Blackrock RD) ~17 mi east of Moran Jct on Buffalo Valley Rd, near the Buffalo Fork River. 18 sites (14 standard + 4 pull-through), vault toilets, water access, corrals/hitching posts (offers stock sites; general campground). Mix of reservable and FCFS. --Claude

name: Atherton Creek Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground on Lower Slide Lake in the Gros Ventre near Kelly; 20 sites, first-come first-served, paved access, RVs to ~30 ft. Picnic tables and fire rings; boat access and trout fishing on the lake. --Claude

name: Bobbie Thomson Campground
note: Medicine Bow NF campground along Douglas Creek near Fox Park, ~8,800 ft. 16 sites first-come first-served, two pull-through, tables/grills, water, vault toilets; access via forest roads (FR 542) with a single-lane bridge. --Claude

name: Boulder Lake Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground at the east end of Boulder Lake SE of Pinedale (end of Boulder Lake Rd). 15 sites, first-come first-served; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, RVs to ~45 ft. Bear food-storage rules apply. --Claude

name: Allred Flat Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground ~20 mi S of Afton on the south side of Salt River Pass, short gravel spur off US-89. 32 first-come first-served sites with pull-throughs (reviewers fit 30-ft+ rigs), non-potable hand-pump water, vault toilets; adjacent to Little White Creek/beaver ponds. --Claude

name: East Fork Campground
note: Bighorn NF campground on the East Fork of Big Goose Creek off FSR 26 (Red Grade/Big Goose Rd), ~2 mi N of Park Reservoir at ~7,600 ft. 11 large single sites, drinking water, vault toilets; sites accommodate RVs/trailers (spurs to ~50 ft per FS). First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Access via Dayton/WY-335 recommended for RVs (Big Horn side road is steep/unpaved). --Claude

name: East Table Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF riverside campground along the Snake River in Snake River Canyon, ~25 mi S of Jackson on US-26/89. 20 standard nonelectric sites (tents/trailers), tables/fire rings/bear boxes, vault toilets; wooded to buffer the highway. 12 sites reservable online, 8 first-come, first-served. Popular fishing & whitewater put-in. --Claude

name: Falls Campground
note: Shoshone NF campground near Brooks Lake Creek Falls, ~25 mi NW of Dubois off US-26/287. 54 sites (Loop A has electric hookups), potable water, tables/fire rings/bear boxes; max spur ~32 ft. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov); cash or check. --Claude

name: Fiddlers Lake Campground
note: Shoshone NF campground on the shore of Fiddlers Lake in the Wind River Mtns, off the Loop Rd (FR 300) SW of Lander at ~9,400 ft. 20 sites, potable water, vault toilets, no hookups; max spur ~40 ft. First-come, first-served (cash/check); open ~June-Sept. --Claude

name: Forest Park Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground on the Greys River, ~34 mi up Greys River Rd (gravel FR 10138). 13 sites shaded by pines on a large loop, hand-pump water, vault toilets; sites accommodate trailers up to ~30 ft. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude
